images.title: Stepping down the powers of 2
images.purpose: Shows the core move of the practice tool: each step down the staircase of powers of 2 divides by 2, giving 2⁰ = 1 and 2 with exponent −1 equal to 1/2.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. A descending staircase of four value cards from top left to bottom right, with an arrow between neighbouring cards.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 4 equal rounded cards placed as descending steps from top left to bottom right. Card texts in order: '2² = 4', '2¹ = 2', '2⁰ = 1', '2⁻¹ = 1/2'; in the last card the raised minus is a true minus sign, not a hyphen. Cards 1 and 2 have a teal (#0072B2) outline, card 3 a thick reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline, card 4 an amber (#E69F00) outline. Between neighbouring cards, exactly 3 small grey curved arrows going down, each labelled '÷ 2'. Exactly 4 cards, 3 arrows.

images.takeaway: Each step down divides by 2, so 2⁰ is 1 and 2⁻¹ is 1/2.
images.description: Shows the core move of the practice tool: each step down the staircase of powers of 2 divides by 2, giving 2⁰ = 1 and 2 with exponent −1 equal to 1/2.
images.context: 4 ÷ 2 = 2, 2 ÷ 2 = 1, 1 ÷ 2 = 1/2. The practice items use the same laws with integer exponents, e.g. 10 to the power −2 × 10 to the power −5 is 10 to the power −7.

image_decisions.why: The practice tool builds a staircase of powers by dividing by the base; this picture shows that manipulation in its simplest state.
